title: Why Sewer Gas Enters the Building: Trap Seal Loss
description: A P-trap relies on a standing water barrier to stop foul sewer gases from entering living spaces. When a drainage system lacks proper venting or experiences negative pressure, the water inside the trap can be sucked out by self-siphonage or induced siphonage. This leaves an open passage for odors and air contaminants to enter the room. Understanding trap seal loss helps plumbers diagnose why drains smell even when there are no visible leaks, pointing to blocked vent stacks, missing air admittance valves, or incorrect pipe installation.

Why Sewer Gas Enters the Building: Trap Seal Loss

A P-trap relies on a standing water barrier to stop foul sewer gases from entering living spaces. When a drainage system lacks proper venting or experiences negative pressure, the water inside the trap can be sucked out by self-siphonage or induced siphonage. This leaves an open passage for odors and air contaminants to enter the room. Understanding trap seal loss helps plumbers diagnose why drains smell even when there are no visible leaks, pointing to blocked vent stacks, missing air admittance valves, or incorrect pipe installation.
